app.description: Governance UI for the MetaFusion account service: users, permission groups, invite codes, OAuth clients and instance settings.
app.footer: Account console: every write goes through metafusion-auth /api/admin/*; the UI never decides locally.
app.subtitle: metafusion-auth · standalone app
app.title: Account console
error.rateLimited: Too many requests (429), please retry later
error.unauthorized: Session expired, please sign in again
groups.allLocalesRequired: All four locale names are required (zh-CN / en-US / zh-TW / ja-JP)
groups.codeInvalid: Invalid group code: lowercase first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or - (2–64 chars)
groups.col.name: Name
groups.deleteConfirm: This deletes group {code}: member references to it disappear and accounts that gained permissions through it lose them. This cannot be undone.
groups.desc: A permission group is a set of permission codes owned by the account service; each subsystem interprets its own codes, and neither the account service nor this UI interprets them.
groups.field.codeHint: Lowercase first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or - (2–64 chars)
groups.field.codeImmutable: The group code anchors member relations and cannot change after creation
groups.permCustomHint: The catalog only lists built-in codes; downstream services may define new ones in the form service.resource.action (up to four segments) or *.
groups.permInvalid: Invalid permission code: service.resource.action (up to four segments) or *
groups.permsDesc: Below is the permission catalog returned by the account service. It is not a whitelist: downstream services may define new codes as long as the format is valid.
groups.title: Permission groups
groups.err.exists: A permission group with this code already exists; pick another code
groups.err.forbidden: Not permitted: this action requires auth.groups.manage
groups.err.invalidCode: Invalid group code: lowercase first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or - (2–64 chars)
groups.err.stripWildcard: The * wildcard cannot be stripped from the admin group
instance.availableGroups: Available permission groups (click to add / remove)
instance.confirmDesc: These changes affect who can register, or how strong the auth endpoints' protection is. They take effect as soon as you confirm:
instance.desc: Instance settings returned by the account service. Writes go through PUT /api/admin/settings (patch semantics: only changed keys are sent), and only settings the service really consumes can be edited.
instance.empty: The account service returned no settings
instance.groupsUnavailable: The group list needs auth.groups.manage and is not visible now: you may type codes directly (only the format is validated; existence cannot be confirmed).
instance.identityDesc: Authorization always follows the permissions returned by the account service (including the * wildcard); this is display only, real checks happen server-side.
instance.identityPermissionsHint: When the permission set is empty, the legacy role=admin fallback applies (same rule as the account service store.Can).
instance.readonlyDesc: Keys the service accepts but nothing consumes, or keys this page has no write entry for. No input is offered on purpose: a field that silently does nothing is worse than one you cannot edit.
instance.setting.auth_rate_limit_enabled: Applies only to auth write endpoints (login/register/refresh) with a fixed window per IP.
instance.setting.auth_rate_limit_per_min: Over the limit returns 429 rate_limited with Retry-After; changes take effect immediately (5s policy cache).
instance.setting.invite_required.hint: When on, registration requires a valid invite code; the account service validates and consumes a use inside the registration transaction.
instance.setting.registration_default_gr: Accounts created through self-registration join these groups automatically.
instance.setting.require_email_verificat: The mail channel is not wired up: reads always answer false and writing true is rejected by the service, so the frontend never shows a verification flow.
instance.title: Instance and settings
instance.why.require_email_verification: The service returns this key, but nothing in the account service enforces it (the mail channel is not wired up): reads always answer false, and writing true is rejected outright (unsupported_setting: require_email_verification). So it is display-only here — turning on a flow that does not exist would only promise users something that never happens.
instance.why.unknown: The service accepts this key, but this page has no write entry for it (probably a newly added setting). Find out what consumes it before adding an input.
instance.writableDesc: For these keys the service accepts writes and code in this repository really consumes them (each one is documented in the source), and changes take effect immediately — the rate-limit policy is read per request, so no restart is needed.
instance.writeHint: Writes go through PUT /api/admin/settings (patch semantics: only changed keys, unknown keys are rejected). Changes that affect admission or protection are confirmed once more before saving.
instance.err.forbidden: Permission denied: this action requires auth.settings.manage (the service decides; hiding the UI is not authorization)
instance.err.groupsFormat: Invalid group code: {code} (lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or -; 2–64 characters)
instance.err.groupsUnknown: No such permission group: {code}. The service silently skips unknown groups at registration, so this is blocked here — create the group under "Permission groups" first, or drop this code.
instance.err.invalidGroupCode: The service rejected a group code: {detail}
instance.err.invalidPayload: Invalid request payload (server error code invalid_payload)
instance.err.invalidSetting: The service does not accept this setting: {detail}
instance.err.rateLimitRange: The rate limit must be an integer between {min} and {max} (same rule as the server)
invites.col.creator: Issuer
invites.desc: Invite ledger and usage. The account service normalises max_uses <= 0 to 1 (max 1000), so there is no unlimited state and the UI does not invent one.
invites.fieldHint: Leave uses empty or 0 to get 1, maximum 1000; days = 0 means no expiry.
invites.revokeConfirm: This revokes invite code {code}: it can no longer be used to register, but accounts created with it are unaffected. This cannot be undone.
invites.title: Invites
invites.err.forbidden: Not permitted: this action requires auth.invites.manage
locale.label: Interface language
oauth.clientIdInvalid: Invalid client_id: lowercase first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or - (3–64 chars)
oauth.createSystemNote: A client created here is a system app (no owner account): it is maintained here only and never shows up in the developer center. Apps that should belong to an account are registered by that account in its own developer center.
oauth.deleteConfirm: This deletes client {name}: its redirect allowlist, scopes and tokens stop working (seeded clients cannot be deleted). This cannot be undone.
oauth.desc: Client governance on the platform admin side: system and third-party apps are both listed here, and system apps are maintained here only. The plaintext secret appears once, in the create or rotate response; the store keeps only a bcrypt hash.
oauth.disableConfirm: This disables {name}: issued tokens stop working immediately at userinfo and verification, and clients must re-authorize after re-enabling.
oauth.disableHint: Disabling invalidates this client's tokens immediately (can be re-enabled)
oauth.field.clientIdHint: Lowercase first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or - (3–64 chars)
oauth.field.name: Display name
oauth.field.redirectUrisHint: One absolute URI per line; only allowlisted redirect_uris are accepted.
oauth.field.scopesHint: The granted set is allowlist ∩ request, narrowed both at code issue and at code exchange.
oauth.field.trustedHint: Trusted clients skip the consent page and get a code directly. Trust is the platform's own identity and should only be given to first-party sites.
oauth.group.systemDesc: Apps registered by the platform itself (no owner account). They are maintained here in the admin console only: the developer center lets each account self-manage the apps it registered, and neither lists nor manages system apps. System apps skip consent, so they are always shown as verified.
oauth.group.thirdPartyDesc: Apps that developers registered themselves in the developer center (they carry an owner account). Verification, disabling, secret rotation and deletion are still governed from this admin console; trust (skip consent) is the platform's own identity and is never given to third parties.
oauth.redirectUrisRequired: At least one redirect URI is required
oauth.rotateConfirm: A new secret will be generated for {name}: the old one stops working immediately and any third party using it can no longer obtain tokens. The new secret is shown once.
oauth.secretWarn: The plaintext secret appears once, in this response only: the store keeps a bcrypt hash, so it cannot be retrieved again after you close this window. Copy and store it now; otherwise you must rotate.
oauth.seededHint: Seeded clients cannot be deleted (the server re-creates them by id on startup)
oauth.title: OAuth clients
oauth.unverifyConfirm: This removes verification from {name}: the consent page shows the “this app has not been verified yet” notice again until it is verified once more.
oauth.unverifyHint: After removing verification, the consent page shows the unverified notice again
oauth.verifyConfirm: This marks {name} as verified: the consent page stops showing the “this app has not been verified yet” notice. Check the app's site and its actual redirect URIs first.
oauth.verifyHint: Once verified, the consent page stops showing the unverified notice
oauth.err.forbidden: Not permitted: this action requires auth.oauth.manage
oauth.err.invalidClientId: Invalid client_id: lowercase first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or - (3–64 chars)
oauth.err.seededClientImmutable: Seeded clients cannot be deleted (the server re-creates them by id on startup)
permission.deniedDesc: This block requires permission code {code}, which your account does not hold.
permission.serverSideHint: The UI only hides it; server-side authorization is the real check. Ask an administrator for the permission group if you need access.
session.failedHint: When the account service is unreachable you are not pushed to the login page; retry once it recovers.
session.loginRequiredDesc: Redirecting to the main site login page; if it does not happen automatically, open /login manually.
users.banConfirm: This bans {username}: login, token refresh and verification are refused immediately, and existing sessions plus third-party tokens are deleted. It can be undone with unban.
users.banSuccess: Banned: the account's sessions and tokens are invalidated at once
users.desc: Member list, roles, ban status and group assignment. Role is a legacy field; authorization follows the permission codes of the groups.
users.field.emailHint: Email may be left empty: the account service falls back to username@findverse.cc
users.groupsForbiddenHint: The group list requires auth.groups.manage and is not available
users.groupsHint: Overwrite semantics: the checked set is the full group set after saving; unchecking removes a group.
users.passwordTooShort: Password length must be between 12 and 72
users.roleChangeWarn: Changing the role rebuilds the member relations from the role defaults: manually assigned groups are cleared (admin → admin; editor → catalog_editor + member; user → member).
users.roleConfirm: The role of {username} will change to {role}. Manually assigned groups are cleared and replaced by the role defaults; this cannot be undone automatically.
users.roleResetNote: Role and groups are two projections of the same fact: changing the role clears and rebuilds the member's manually assigned groups.
users.selfBanHint: You cannot ban yourself (the server returns cannot_ban_self)
users.title: User governance
users.unbanConfirm: This unbans {username}: the account can sign in and refresh tokens again.
users.err.cannotBanSelf: You cannot ban yourself: you would need someone else to undo it
users.err.cannotBanSoleAdmin: You cannot ban the last administrator who can still sign in
users.err.cannotDemoteSoleAdmin: You cannot demote the last administrator
users.err.invalidPasswordLength: Password length must be between 12 and 72
users.err.invalidRole: Role must be user / editor / admin
